# Running the Loop {#sec-running-the-loop}

![](images/ch08-cover-map.svg){fig-alt="The prospective cache record stops before dispatch; the separate retained array record reaches a limited technical stop; neither closes a design loop."}

::: {.epigraph}
> "Beware of bugs in the above code; I have only proved it correct, not tried it."
>
> — Donald E. Knuth, *Notes on the van Emde Boas Construction of Priority Deques* (1977) [@Knuth1977PriorityDeques]
:::

An architecture study can produce a useful stopping decision without closing a design loop. This chapter compares two such records to distinguish what was planned, what ran, and what an architect can conclude from each.

The prospective mobile XR cache study translates a 3\ W system objective into a single pre-register-transfer level (RTL) decision on L2 capacity. It stops before tool dispatch because the required physical derivation rules and toolchain bindings are incomplete. The specification supports no measured cache result.

The separate [retained systolic-array study](https://github.com/harvard-edge/arch2/tree/f5516e52e66243c2d753191e350a5cfac56c83af/labs/examples/ai_systolic_array_study) uses SCALE-Sim (a cycle-level systolic array simulator) [@RajEtAl2025ScaleSimV3] to evaluate general matrix multiplication (GEMM) kernels. Its preregistered twelve-event sweep returns an exact ranking tie, refutes the generative model's directional hypothesis, and stops with a technical recommendation awaiting a human decision. No return changes the sweep's plan.

A comparison of the records separates architecture outcomes, AI contributions, mechanism tests, and stopping rules. Neither record supplies the evidence missing from the other. A final hypothetical example shows how returned evidence could trigger redesign and close a loop without guaranteeing a successful architecture.

## Prospective Cache Design Study

Machine-usable representations (@sec-data-representations-world-models), smallest sufficient methods (@sec-methods-generation-prediction-optimization), sandboxed environments (@sec-architecture-environments-tool-interfaces), and qualified feedback (@sec-feedback-verification-trust) support different parts of a design study. A design loop closes only when returned evidence alters the represented state and triggers a subsequent action (@sec-design-loop-no-longer-scales). Specifying these parts is therefore a prerequisite for execution, not evidence that a loop has run.

Sizing a mobile XR Level-2 cache invites a simulation sweep across capacities. Before such a sweep can answer the architecture question, however, each capacity needs a defined hardware organization and an evaluation path that can test its performance and power consequences. The first study specifies a comparison under a strict 3\ W thermal envelope. It names the baseline, instruction set architecture (ISA) invariants, physical derivation rules, and stopping criteria that must be fixed before dispatch, while exposing the bindings that remain unfinished.

The study stops within Implement, before any tool invocation. Its declaration lets us identify the missing derivation rules, executable tool bindings, and cost accounting without treating the proposed measurements as returned evidence.

::: {.callout-lighthouse title="Where is the Physical Silicon Flow?"}
**Context.** Establishing Lighthouse's physical feasibility would require a bound synthesis and physical-design flow with checks appropriate to the implementation claim. The cache plan here has not reached that work.

**Application.** The separate SCALE-Sim array sweep lets students inspect preregistration, budget accounting, returned metrics, and a stopping rule in an executed record. It supplies no cache measurements or physical validation for Lighthouse, and its fixed sweep does not adapt its proposals to returned evidence.

**Outcome.** Students can trace how each study reaches its stopping boundary without mistaking either record for a closed loop. A later hypothetical instruction-design example shows the additional feedback step that would close a loop; it is a teaching illustration, not a third executed study.
:::

### Architectural Decision

Expanding Level-2 cache capacity inside a strict 3\ W thermal design power (TDP) budget trades off off-chip memory latency against static leakage power and physical silicon area. For the Lighthouse mobile XR subsystem (@sec-moonshot), the prospective study chooses TSMC N3E, a 3\ nm-class process, as its implementation target and asks whether a larger Level-2 cache should advance to RTL evaluation. This is a chosen process requirement, not a bound technology model or evidence of physical feasibility. The planned comparison across the eight requirement domains (@sec-intent-vs-spec) would hold the RV64GCV ISA contract, vector CPU and neural processing unit (NPU) compute topologies, XR workload snapshots, and runtime compiler passes fixed, isolating L2 capacity as the single swept variable: a 2\ MiB baseline against 3\ MiB and 4\ MiB candidates. These capacities define the distinct architectural objects within the prospective study, though they remain specification targets rather than generated RTL instances or measured artifacts in the repository.

Architects frequently treat cache capacity as an integer knob in a configuration file. In silicon, however, an additional megabyte requires significant physical resources; it is a physical array of millions of static random-access memory (SRAM) bitcells, wordline drivers, sense amplifiers, and multiplexers placed, routed, and powered within tight timing and area envelopes. A candidate capacity of 3\ MiB needs a legal construction, but does not inherently require non-uniform banks. A different number of equal-capacity banks may be possible if the declared indexing policy can address them. The derivation rule must specify the organization and record its hit-latency and floorplan consequences.

The declaration below fixes associativity, line size, indexing and replacement policies, miss status holding register (MSHR) count, ports, hit-latency allocation, and process, voltage, and temperature (PVT) conditions.[^fn-pvt-corners-c08] Given those controlled inputs and a requested capacity, the derivation rule must determine set and bank counts, subarray geometry, tag and data arrays, periphery, and SRAM macro composition. The resulting layout and access path must then be checked against the fixed timing and area limits. The indexing and port-arbitration implementation must remain consistent with the declared policies; bank hot-spotting under spatially correlated XR camera frames is behavior to test, not something an indexing function alone guarantees away. If a capacity cannot be implemented without changing a controlled parameter, that change requires a revised study declaration rather than an undocumented adjustment.

Physical consequences can compound under thermal and workload stress. The proposed mobile XR workload assumes streaming 120\ Hz sensor video buffers and concurrent spatial tracking, which would compete for cache lines. An undersized Level-2 cache could let streaming frames evict active neural network weights and tracking state. The resulting capacity misses could fill the MSHR queue and increase memory traffic, delaying execution enough to miss the strict 8.33\ ms frame deadline[^fn-xr-workload-c08] chosen for the prospective subsystem requirements (@sec-intent-vs-spec). Conversely, expanding the cache to 4\ MiB adds bitcells and therefore a potential leakage cost, which can grow at higher operating temperatures and consume part of the chosen 3\ W subsystem envelope before dynamic switching energy is counted. These are competing risks to test: the unexecuted cache study establishes neither a deadline violation nor the leakage magnitude for any capacity.

The planned fixed architectural state extends beyond the cache itself to network-on-chip (NoC) configurations, the 2\ GHz host RV64GCV vector CPU microarchitecture, the just-in-time (JIT) compiler and runtime environment, the RISC-V software image, and an XR workload snapshot with stable frame boundaries. These are prospective choices that the executable study would have to bind. Because the repository currently lacks both the structural derivation rule and bound values for controlled cache and PVT parameters, the comparison cannot yet execute.

The planned evaluation path spans the tool categories of @sec-architecture-environments-tool-interfaces. It names gem5 for full-system simulation, Verilator for simulation of RTL models, CACTI for SRAM area modeling, Yosys for logic synthesis, OpenROAD for physical implementation and timing analysis, RedHawk-SC for power-integrity analysis, and Ramulator for dynamic random-access memory (DRAM) timing. These are proposed roles, not a connected or qualified toolchain.

Other named elements describe what an engine would consume or model. Unified Power Format (IEEE 1801 UPF) expresses power intent; SystemVerilog Assertions (SVA) express properties for a verification engine, with bounded model checking (BMC) among the proposed checks. Universal Chiplet Interconnect Express (UCIe) and Compute Express Link (CXL) specify interconnect behavior and interfaces rather than supplying executable interconnect models. The required power-aware checking engines, supported assertion flow, interconnect models, and thermal-analysis path remain to be selected and bound. None of the proposed tool roles is connected to executable study scripts in the repository.

The proposed architecture claim is that a larger Level-2 cache reduces 99th-percentile frame times by eliminating capacity misses while satisfying power, area, access-time, and coherence constraints. Testing this claim requires matched frame observations showing that resolving capacity misses improves tail latency under fixed workload and software conditions. Because the legal space contains only the baseline and two discrete alternatives, the study relies on direct evaluation (@sec-methods-generation-prediction-optimization) rather than generative search. The SRAM model acts as a standard tool-path component rather than an AI module. Once the tool path is operational, direct evaluation is sufficient to compare these three capacities. The result could recommend at most one capacity for RTL evaluation; it would not authorize tapeout.

### Execution Prerequisites

Translating an abstract architectural proposal into a reproducible simulation job requires converting high-level capacity targets into concrete, hardware-derived configuration structures. Candidate capacities of 3\ MiB or 4\ MiB dictate physical SRAM set counts, bank topologies, array geometries, and hit-latency profiles that must obey invariant physical rules. Before dispatching any simulation jobs, the experimental framework must explicitly declare its candidate requests, cycle-level simulator requirements, dispatch conditions, required telemetry schemas, functional checks, call-count limits, and failure-handling procedures (@tbl-cache-run-declaration). Without these operational prerequisites locked in advance, execution cannot be reproduced, audited, or distinguished from ad hoc manual tuning.

| **Run parameter** | **Declared mobile XR cache study work** |
| - | - |
| **Candidate requests** | Prepare one complete request to the SRAM model under declared PVT conditions for 2\ MiB baseline, 3\ MiB, and 4\ MiB candidates. Treat `l2.capacity` as sole swept parameter while strictly holding associativity, line size, indexing, replacement, MSHR count, ports, hit-latency allocation, and PVT fixed. A prospectively bound rule must derive set count, bank count, layout geometry, periphery, and SRAM macro composition directly from capacity. All controlled and derived values remain retained alongside SRAM-model and technology identities. |
| **Cycle-level requests** | Rerun 2\ MiB baseline alongside eligible candidates through cycle-level simulator, including cache and power models while holding declared XR workload snapshot, software image, and hardware/software identities strictly fixed. |
| **Dispatch condition** | No request is eligible until policy parameters and capacity-derived choices are bound. A cycle-level request becomes eligible for execution only when `(return_complete == true) && (schema_valid == true) && (area_mm2 <= 1.5) && (access_time_ns <= 2.5)`. This condition authorizes simulation dispatch without independently validating a measurement or rejecting a candidate. |
| **Required returns** | Retain SRAM area, access time, dynamic energy, leakage, matched frame records, frame-time inputs, and 99th-percentile frame time. Include cache miss classification, subsystem power, tool versions, model identities, translated inputs, warnings, failures, cryptographic hashes, data lineage, and precise accounting records covering wait times, run times, compute resource use, license checkout, storage, and human setup time. |
| **Checks** | Require identical ISA-visible outputs and standard functional regressions for every capacity. Demand zero coherence-invariant failures, subsystem power (dynamic plus leakage) capped at 3\ W, total cache macro area $\le 1.5\text{ mm}^2$, and modeled access time $\le 2.5\text{ ns}$. Require uncertainty-qualified frame-time comparisons against rerun baseline. |
| **Failure handling** | Refuse invalid evaluation requests prior to simulation invocation. Distinguish timeouts, cancellations, infrastructure failures, state corruption, missing outputs, and parser errors. Retry attempts link to parent attempt, deduct from budget, and launch from a freshly generated clean state without altering candidate architecture. |
| **Budget** | Permit three SRAM model evaluations and restrict cycle-level executions to at most four, explicitly accounting for infrastructure reruns. Exclude RTL synthesis and physical signoff from exploratory budget. Define accounting for wait/run times, compute consumption, license constraints, tool utilization, storage costs, and human effort. |
| **Stopping** | Stop simulation attempts when queue-wait or run-time deadlines expire. Halt study upon resolving architectural decision, exhausting eligible capacities, consuming cycle-level budget, breaching project deadline, lacking required tools, or finding no alternative meeting SRAM physical limits. |
| **Decision** | Require uncertainty-qualified frame-time improvement strictly greater than zero. Prospectively define statistical estimator, confidence procedure, and practical performance margins prior to dispatch. Recommend at most one capacity for RTL evaluation if required checks pass cleanly and qualified comparison proves declared improvement. |
: **Run declarations expose evaluated parameters and experimental bounds.** The declaration identifies the intended requests, necessary returns, functional checks, call-count limits, and decision criteria, highlighting that cache-policy bindings, derived-structure rules, statistical procedures, cost accounting, numeric deadlines, and the executable measurement path remain unfinished. {#tbl-cache-run-declaration tbl-colwidths="[25,75]"}

The declaration fixes the required improvement direction but leaves the statistical procedure unfinished. Before dispatch, the study must define the estimator, confidence procedure, and practical performance margins alongside the candidate parameters. Changing workload trace windows, simulation seeds, or tool constraints after seeing which candidate benefits would undermine the baseline comparison.[^fn-fda-preregistration-c08] A justified change can motivate a new comparison, but it must remain distinguishable from the one originally declared.

[^fn-fda-preregistration-c08]: **Clinical trial preregistration parallel**: Clinical-trial registration records a protocol and its primary and secondary outcome variables before a trial begins, making outcome switching after results are seen easier to detect [@NosekEtAl2018Preregistration]. In computer architecture, locking trace windows, workload seeds, and electronic design automation (EDA) synthesis constraints prior to execution serves a similar purpose in preserving baseline comparative integrity.

### Specification Audit

The inventory in @tbl-cache-evidence-inventory separates prospective specifications and teaching fixtures from true execution traces. Prospective specifications declare what a study intends to compare, while teaching fixtures illustrate how measurement pipelines behave; neither provides empirical evidence of hardware performance. Independently replayable execution evidence requires retained invocations, serialized state, outputs, identities, and lineage sufficient for an external reviewer to reconstruct what ran. Retained artifacts divide into specification targets (controlled cache parameters and declared tool roles), author-constructed teaching fixtures (illustrative SRAM and simulator entries), and executed evidence packages. Retained specifications and teaching fixtures clarify methodology, but they cannot support a measured cache result.

| **Retained item** | **Evidence class** | **What it supports** | **What remains absent** |
| - | - | - | - |
| mobile XR cache study, current design revision, controlled-state identities, and the three cache candidates | Specification identity | The cache question, comparator, intended controlled state, permitted capacity change, required measurements, call-count limits, stopping categories, and intended pre-register-transfer level (RTL) decision. | Bound policy parameters, capacity-derived cache structure, retained candidate artifacts, executable requests, runs, measurements, and a cache disposition. |
| Run declaration and its declared tool roles | Specification identity | The intended request translation, dispatch condition, return schema, failure handling, call-count limits, and tool responsibilities. | Numeric deadlines, a cost-accounting procedure, bound executables, wrapper and parser versions, exact inputs, host state, commands, logs, outputs, and realized cost. |
| Constructed SRAM and simulator entries plus a design-loop card that summarizes the proposed question, state, returns, checks, and decision | Author-constructed teaching fixture | Illustrative area, access-time, power, failure, return, and summary properties that a study record might retain. | Terminal and parser status, exact requests, raw artifacts, state identities, dispatch evidence, lineage, realized cost, and any measured cache result. |
| Retained cache execution package | Executed evidence | None. No such package is present. | Candidate artifacts, tool requests, raw outputs, parsed measurements, hashes, lineage, costs, qualified comparisons, and a decision record. |
: **Evidence inventories retain complete study specifications.** Similar-looking identifiers across chapters do not convert constructed specification entries into executed evidence. {#tbl-cache-evidence-inventory tbl-colwidths="[28,18,27,27]"}

These specification entries and teaching fixtures clarify design intent, declare tool obligations, and establish operational structure, yet they leave the physical feasibility, timing closure,[^fn-timing-closure-c08] and empirical performance of each capacity candidate entirely unmeasured. Without executed runs and retained output artifacts, the study remains a methodological blueprint rather than an empirical evaluation.

::: {.callout-design-principle title="Decouple Intent from Executed Evidence"}
**The principle:** Keep architectural intent distinct from executed evidence. A prospective specification frames a search space and fixes what a study would compare; it establishes nothing about how a candidate behaves.

**The application:** Only an executed run returns evidence, and that evidence is bounded by what the executing tool actually models. Conflating an unexecuted plan with a modeled outcome, or a modeled outcome with a physical one, destroys empirical validity.
:::

### Analytical Judgments

Evaluating an unexecuted study requires decoupling its structural status from its technical conclusions across four analytical criteria (@tbl-cache-judgments). The architecture outcome remains unresolved, the AI contribution and hardware mechanism remain untested, and the study halts because execution prerequisites are missing rather than because budget was exhausted or a candidate failed. Decoupling these four axes prevents misinterpreting an unexecuted tool path as a completed architectural evaluation. Unlike the system-level judgments of @sec-evaluating-agentic-architect that evaluate a complete workflow across multiple iterations, these four criteria isolate what a single record establishes. A record has to answer here before a system can be judged there.

| **Judgment** | **Cache conclusion** | **Evidence boundary** |
| - | - | - |
| **Architecture outcome** | Unresolved. No capacity advances, and none is rejected. | No retained cache candidate was executed, the baseline was not rerun, and no required comparison was qualified. |
| **AI contribution** | Not tested. | Direct evaluation with no added learned method was the declared approach. No AI-versus-conventional comparison exists. |
| **Mechanism** | Untested. | No retained miss classifications or matched frame observations test whether reduced capacity misses change 99th-percentile frame time. |
| **Stopping** | Stop before execution because the implementation, measurement, and dispatch prerequisites are unavailable. | The declared budget was not consumed. If the cache decision remains worth pursuing, a new run requires bound policy and derived cache choices, numeric deadlines, a cost-accounting procedure, candidate artifacts, tool bindings, request translation, and an executable measurement path. Deferral, cancellation, or reformulation remain legitimate. |
: **Cache decisions remain open across four distinct technical criteria.** Missing execution leaves the architecture outcome unresolved, the explicit no-added-method choice leaves any AI contribution untested, missing empirical observations leave the hardware mechanism untested, and absent execution prerequisites dictate the stopping point. {#tbl-cache-judgments tbl-colwidths="[20,38,42]"}

The stop occurs before execution. The study supplies no basis for advancing a capacity to RTL evaluation, including the baseline, whose behavior also remains unmeasured here. The architect can defer, cancel, or complete the missing prerequisites without declaring any capacity a winner or a failure.

## Executed Systolic-Array Study {#sec-executed-scale-study}

The second record reaches execution and completes its preregistered simulation budget, then stops at a local tie. Where the prospective cache study addresses memory-hierarchy capacity under system-level constraints, this executed systolic-array experiment focuses on compute-engine microarchitecture within a dedicated neural processing unit (NPU) accelerator. Its fixed interfaces fit the scope of AI-driven optimization (@fig-ch01-three-layers-ai-integration), but no returned result changes its proposals or evaluation plan. The retained sweep therefore does not close a design loop.

Compute arrays are an attractive target for architectural exploration. A systolic processing element (PE) grid has uniform clocking, regular register-to-register interconnect, and deterministic cycle behavior, so a cycle-level simulator or spreadsheet that tracks multiply-accumulate (MAC) throughput under idealized assumptions is easy to build. These idealized assumptions limit the accuracy of such analytical sweeps. An array without matched memory bandwidth starves for activations or stalls on output writebacks, and its processing elements sit idle while consuming clock-tree power; DRAM bank conflicts, network-on-chip (NoC) serialization, SRAM writeback contention, and thermal dissipation sit outside the model that ranked it.

This study explores legal PE geometries in SCALE-Sim [@RajEtAl2025ScaleSimV3]. Its fixed configuration makes the comparison inspectable: the reader can trace each proposal through the same workload, dataflow, score, and stopping rule, then ask what those choices left unmeasured.

### Freezing Candidates

Preregistering an architectural experiment locks the hypothesis, baseline configuration, and interpretation rules before simulation tools return a single performance cycle [@NosekEtAl2018Preregistration]. In the retained systolic-array package ([`arch2_scale_ai_study_v1`](https://github.com/harvard-edge/arch2/tree/f5516e52e66243c2d753191e350a5cfac56c83af/labs/examples/ai_systolic_array_study)), the study freezes legal processing-element geometries, evaluation metrics, simulation budgets, rejection checks, and decision margins prior to candidate selection.

For the matrix product $C = AB$, let $A$ have dimensions $M \times K$, $B$ have dimensions $K \times N$, and the output $C$ have dimensions $M \times N$. Thus $M$ and $N$ count output rows and columns, while $K$ is the shared dimension over which each output element accumulates products. These are workload dimensions, distinct from the hardware array's rows and columns. The simulator maps the matrix operations onto that smaller grid, reusing its processing elements across successive tiles when a matrix dimension exceeds the available hardware.

The study evaluates systolic-array geometries across three synthetic GEMM layers with $(M, N, K)$ dimension tuples of $(128, 128, 256)$, $(64, 192, 128)$, and $(32, 128, 192)$. These are isolated matrix multiplications under one fixed workload and simulator configuration, rather than complete traces from an identified spatial-tracking pipeline. SCALE-Sim [@RajEtAl2025ScaleSimV3] models PE array mechanics, line buffers, and SRAM traffic under a Weight-Stationary dataflow.[^fn-weight-stationary-c08] Setting `UseRamulatorTrace = False` excludes memory-channel contention, row-buffer hits, bank conflicts, and DRAM command timing from the retained runs.

The execution setup varies array height and width in SCALE-Sim 3.0.0 while holding the dataflow, each of the three on-chip SRAM capacities at 128\ KiB, and configured interface bandwidth values of 64 fixed. Python wrapper scripts (`run_scalesim.py`) dispatch the simulator, ingest CSV workload files, and return structured performance summaries alongside DRAM bandwidth reports (`BANDWIDTH_REPORT.csv`). These design choices derive directly from the package's [frozen preregistration](https://github.com/harvard-edge/arch2/blob/f5516e52e66243c2d753191e350a5cfac56c83af/labs/examples/ai_systolic_array_study/context/pre_registration.yaml) and retained per-run configurations.

Under the Weight-Stationary dataflow, weight tiles stay resident inside local PE registers while activation values stream horizontally through the array and partial sums accumulate vertically down the columns [@RajEtAl2025ScaleSimV3]. The retained study enforces a 1,024-processing-element hardware limit, a 90,000-cycle performance cutoff, and a mandatory 32 by 32 baseline. The protocol allocates exactly four simulator evaluation events per proposal arm alongside four shared mechanism-probe events, basing every architectural judgment on cycle counts rather than wall-clock time. A fixed aspect-ratio heuristic, a few lines of deterministic code rather than a tuned search, serves as the budget-matched comparator. The comparator is deliberately modest, because the object of the study is the matched protocol and not the difficulty of the search. Dividing execution latency by fractional layer utilization combines execution speed and hardware efficiency into a single, lower-is-better metric:

$$
S = \frac{\text{total cycles}}{\bar{U}_{\text{frac}}}
$$

where $\bar{U}_{\text{frac}} = \bar{U}_{\%} / 100 \in (0, 1]$ represents the arithmetic mean fractional layer utilization.

The evaluation runner computes this score directly from the retained SCALE-Sim outputs. This score operates as a study-specific proxy; it is not a direct physical measurement, a classical area-delay product, or a universal accelerator metric. The runner calculates total cycles by summing the `Total Cycles` column, excluding the separate prefetch-inclusive column. To determine average layer utilization, it computes the arithmetic mean of the three per-layer `Overall Util %` values (rather than the `Compute Util %`), giving each workload layer equal weight. Consequently, the score does not explicitly penalize processing-element count, physical die area, or modeled memory traffic. Under the frozen decision rule, a lower score ranks a candidate better for this comparison, and a legal nonbaseline candidate clears the 1% support margin when $S_{\text{candidate}} \leq 0.99 \times S_{32\times32}$ (where exact equality at this threshold constitutes a passing result).

The test framework constructs both evaluation arms from the identical three-row CSV workload, tracking a layer name alongside the $M$, $N$, and $K$ dimensions for each dense GEMM. Systolic-array rows and columns are restricted to the set of 8, 16, 32, 64, and 128, with their product constrained not to exceed the 1,024 processing-element budget. After inserting the mandatory 32 by 32 baseline, the runner holds the workload, layout, SCALE-Sim configuration, dataflow, SRAM capacities, bandwidth parameters, performance deadlines, legality checks, and local score fixed for every candidate architecture.

The candidate generation roles are equally constrained. The generative model is permitted to return three unique, legal nonbaseline shapes and a supporting mechanism hypothesis. However, it is strictly forbidden from invoking SCALE-Sim, waiving hardware checks, formulating the final recommendation, or making the architecture decision autonomously. Conversely, the deterministic heuristic filters out the baseline and ranks every legal systolic shape using three criteria: first by decreasing processing-element count, then by the absolute log2 distance between the candidate's columns-to-rows ratio and the aggregate workload $N$-to-$M$ ratio, and finally by increasing row and column counts. Programmatically selecting the top three shapes from this sorted list, plus the baseline, guarantees that each proposal arm receives exactly four simulator events.

The rule can be checked by hand from the three declared layers. Their aggregate $N$-to-$M$ ratio is $448/224 = 2$, and among the five 1,024-element shapes the log2 distances of columns-to-rows from that ratio are 1 for 16 by 64 and for 32 by 32, 3 for 8 by 128 and for 64 by 16, and 5 for 128 by 8. Dropping the baseline and breaking the tie at distance 3 by ascending row count yields 16 by 64, 8 by 128, and 64 by 16, which is the heuristic arm the record retains.

### Execution Chronology

Even when an evaluation methodology is prospectively locked, real-world tool execution introduces interface errors, schema mismatches, and infrastructure retries that alter the chronological path to evidence. The retained execution history captures these operational realities, documenting an initial schema validation failure followed by a corrected model invocation, twelve successful simulator runs, and four independent analytical judgments (@fig-array-study-workflow). Incorporating explicit error-recovery loops within the workflow preserves prospective experimental integrity when interface failures occur.

![**Retained execution workflow and fourfold architectural interpretation.** The top execution sequence progresses from a frozen plan through schema validation, candidate selection, simulation execution in SCALE-Sim (a cycle-level systolic array simulator) [@RajEtAl2025ScaleSimV3], and record interpretation, with a pre-inference schema repair loop. The interpreted record branches into four independent analytical judgments: architecture outcome (no nonbaseline shape clears margin), study-local AI contribution (no advantage over heuristic), mechanism status (directional reversal fails), and stopping point (technical stop retaining 32 by 32).](images/fig-array-study-workflow){#fig-array-study-workflow width="80%" fig-alt="An architecture workflow freezes a plan and validates a proposal schema before selecting candidates, checking legality, and executing simulator runs. A failed schema returns through repair and revalidation. One shared stem from the interpreted record then branches to four boxes for the architecture outcome, study-local AI contribution, mechanism status, and stopping judgment."}

Each transition (@tbl-array-chronology) is recorded, from the preregistration freeze through schema rejection, repair, proposal generation, simulator execution, and technical handoff. This timeline exposes both what the execution logs verify and what provenance data remains missing, including omitted random seeds, unrecorded currency costs, and absent repository commit hashes.

: **Array chronologies record execution events and configuration changes.** The [preregistration](https://github.com/harvard-edge/arch2/blob/f5516e52e66243c2d753191e350a5cfac56c83af/labs/examples/ai_systolic_array_study/context/pre_registration.yaml), [model provenance](https://github.com/harvard-edge/arch2/blob/f5516e52e66243c2d753191e350a5cfac56c83af/labs/examples/ai_systolic_array_study/recorded/model/provenance.json), [execution provenance](https://github.com/harvard-edge/arch2/blob/f5516e52e66243c2d753191e350a5cfac56c83af/labs/examples/ai_systolic_array_study/recorded/reference/execution_provenance.json), and [study results](https://github.com/harvard-edge/arch2/blob/f5516e52e66243c2d753191e350a5cfac56c83af/labs/examples/ai_systolic_array_study/recorded/reference/study_results.json) collectively document one schema setup failure before a valid model call, twelve completed simulator events, and no authorized acceptance or rejection. {#tbl-array-chronology tbl-colwidths="[24,38,38]"}

Read end to end, the chronology also bounds what the study cost in time. From the preregistration freeze at 18:19:48 UTC to the last simulator event at 18:31:42 UTC is about twelve minutes of wall clock, of which the model call took 32.90 seconds and the twelve simulator events 19.05 seconds; the remaining minutes fall between recorded events, and the record does not say what filled them.

The two arms also require different kinds of effort, which the record measures incompletely. The model arm consumed 13.2k input and 1.4k output tokens, 32.90 seconds of wall time, and an unrecorded amount of prompt and schema authoring; the heuristic arm required the few lines of deterministic code that state its rule. A performance tie therefore does not establish a tie in total cost. The missing currency and human-effort records prevent quantifying the difference.

Because the response-format service rejects the schema prior to model inference, the record treats this failure as a routine issue in request translation and interface validation. Throughout this process, the core architecture question, legal shape set, hardware score, and evaluation budget remain unchanged. The amendment therefore functions as a necessary request repair within the boundaries of the study. However, because the repository lacks the original schema body and the explicit service response, reviewers cannot confirm that the amendment preserved the request's intended architectural meaning.

The [model provenance](https://github.com/harvard-edge/arch2/blob/f5516e52e66243c2d753191e350a5cfac56c83af/labs/examples/ai_systolic_array_study/recorded/model/provenance.json) records invocation parameters and interface metadata, but omits the final serving state and sampling settings. In addition, a prompt hash mismatch between preregistration and surviving logs prevents cryptographic verification of the exact input context. Finally, the simulator provenance records the software stack but fails to bind the runner to a specific repository commit, container image, or dependency lock.[^fn-provenance-tracking-c08] Extensive full-system simulation studies emphasize that unrecorded configuration differences can alter hardware performance outcomes [@GutierrezEtAl2014SourcesOfError]. While this context does not diagnose an error in the run, it prevents confirmation of which missing identity might have altered the final execution result.

[^fn-provenance-tracking-c08]: **Provenance tracking details**: Invocations accessed OpenAI via Codex CLI 0.144.4 (alias `gpt-5.4`), consuming 13.2k input tokens and 1.4k output tokens without recorded seed or temperature. Preregistered prompt hash (`ec12df...`) differs from the surviving prompt file hash (`36e016...`). Simulator runs executed on macOS 26.4 (arm64) using Python 3.11.15 and SCALE-Sim (a cycle-level systolic array simulator) 3.0.0.

Within the retained array directory, the package lacks an independently preserved validation dataset artifact. The retained record does not establish that reference integrity, execution replay, or focused hardware tests were independently verified. Its files and current replay pathways remain inspectable, so a separately documented rerun can test what the available package computes. Such a rerun would still share the workload, scoring mechanism, and architectural assumptions unless it explicitly introduced independent checks; missing historical identities would prevent establishing that it exactly reproduced the original execution. The executed record also lacks study-local independent analytical models, RTL validation, or cross-simulator checks to anchor software modeling against cycle-exact field-programmable gate array (FPGA) RTL behavior using platforms such as FireSim [@KarandikarEtAl2018FireSim]. The study also omitted an analytical fold-count verification check. While a newly frozen mechanism study could introduce that check as future work, the mapping discussion below serves as an expert interpretation of the tagged simulator implementation rather than executed evidence. These provenance gaps prevent establishing an exact historical replay and limit causal attribution. The retained outputs can still support the narrower comparison actually computed under the recorded workload, simulator configuration, local score, and checks, provided the gaps are carried directly into that claim.

### Local Simulator Outputs

With the execution history established, the next question is what the returned measurements say about the candidate shapes. Each proposal arm evaluated the 32 by 32 baseline alongside three alternatives under the same simulator-event budget. That comparison can establish whether the model found a better local candidate than the fixed heuristic; it cannot establish readiness for physical synthesis.
The simulator returns make that comparison explicit (@tbl-array-results). Across eight simulation runs evaluating five unique array geometries, the model-generated proposals match the deterministic aspect-ratio heuristic's best score. The 32 by 32 baseline and the 16 by 64 candidate achieve identical execution latencies of 13,917 cycles and matching layer utilization of 41.196%, yielding an identical local score of 33,782.40. Both arms tie at this score, while the extreme 8 by 128 aspect ratio returns more cycles and lower array utilization. Under equal simulator-event budgets, generative proposals provide no local performance advantage over the fixed heuristic. This tie does not establish physical equivalence or show that additional computation would resolve the choice.

| **Arm** | **Shape and source** | **PE count (author-derived)** | **Cycles** | **Average layer utilization** | **Local score** | **Result within arm** |
| - | - | ---: | -: | -: | -: | - |
| Model | 32 by 32 baseline | 1,024 | 13,917 | 41.196% | 33,782.40 | Tied best |
| Model | 16 by 64 proposal | 1,024 | 13,917 | 41.196% | 33,782.40 | Tied best |
| Model | 8 by 128 proposal | 1,024 | 19,405 | 29.704% | 65,327.45 | Ranked worse |
| Model | 32 by 16 proposal | 512 | 25,277 | 45.438% | 55,629.61 | Ranked worse |
| Heuristic | 32 by 32 baseline | 1,024 | 13,917 | 41.196% | 33,782.40 | Tied best |
| Heuristic | 16 by 64 proposal | 1,024 | 13,917 | 41.196% | 33,782.40 | Tied best |
| Heuristic | 8 by 128 proposal | 1,024 | 19,405 | 29.704% | 65,327.45 | Ranked worse |
| Heuristic | 64 by 16 proposal | 1,024 | 17,757 | 32.294% | 54,985.25 | Ranked worse |
: **The two proposal arms tie under equalized simulator-event budgets.** Neither evaluation branch discovers an evaluated nonbaseline shape that clears the recorded 1% performance margin over the default 32 by 32 array. Values derive directly from the [retained study results](https://github.com/harvard-edge/arch2/blob/f5516e52e66243c2d753191e350a5cfac56c83af/labs/examples/ai_systolic_array_study/recorded/reference/study_results.json) rather than post-fabrication silicon measurements. Processing-element counts are calculated by multiplying rows by columns. {#tbl-array-results tbl-colwidths="[10,18,14,12,16,14,16]"}

The 32 by 16 proposal deploys 512 processing elements, whereas the 32 by 32, 16 by 64, 8 by 128, and 64 by 16 configurations each deploy exactly 1,024. Consequently, array shape and overall processing-element count vary simultaneously during the 32 by 16 comparison. A hardware design with 512 processing elements exhibits a different resource trade-off profile compared to standard shapes using 1,024 elements. However, because the study does not measure explicit area or energy consequences of this architectural discrepancy, the retained result remains a score-only local hardware outcome. The best evaluated nonbaseline configuration, the 16 by 64 array, exactly matches the 32 by 32 baseline in total execution cycles, average layer utilization, and final local score, failing to clear the predefined architectural change margin. In addition, the 8 by 128, 32 by 16, and 64 by 16 designs all rank worse under the frozen scoring metric, yielding a no-change outcome across five uniquely evaluated hardware shapes (though this result alone does not prove that the 32 by 32 layout is globally optimal among all legally permitted dimensions).

The study yields two separable empirical findings across candidate scoring and directional mechanism validation (@fig-ai-study-result). Candidate scoring evaluates whether model proposals outperform a fixed heuristic under equal simulator budgets (@fig-ai-study-result a), while the mechanism probe tests whether swapping matrix dimensions $M$ and $N$ reverses relative array performance (@fig-ai-study-result b). While the proposal ranking yields a functional tie, the targeted mechanism test fails its declared performance reversal. Because these two results investigate different architectural questions, the tied evaluation score cannot serve as supporting evidence for the model's directional explanation.

(b) Tracking of the mechanism probe, showing that the 16 by 64 array remains ahead of the 64 by 16 shape across both original and transposed ($M$ and $N$ swapped) workloads (23.5k vs 25.5k), directly refuting the predicted performance reversal. Values derive from retained SCALE-Sim (a cycle-level systolic array simulator) simulator logs [@RajEtAl2025ScaleSimV3] rather than physical silicon measurements.

_root = Path(_ap.__file__).resolve().parents[2]
result_path = _root / "labs/examples/ai_systolic_array_study/recorded/reference/study_results.json"
result = json.loads(result_path.read_text(encoding="utf-8"))

arm_runs = [r for r in result["evaluations"] if r["arm"] in {"model", "conventional"}]
probe_runs = [r for r in result["evaluations"] if r["arm"] == "mechanism_probe"]

shape_labels = {
    "model_baseline_32x32": "M  32×32 baseline",

    "heuristic_64x16": "H  64×16",

fig, (ax1, ax2) = plt.subplots(1, 2, figsize=(5.6, 2.65), gridspec_kw={"width_ratios": [1.35, 1]})
fig.subplots_adjust(left=0.22, right=0.985, top=0.82, bottom=0.22, wspace=0.42)

labels = [shape_labels[r["candidate_id"]] for r in arm_runs]
scores = [r["decision_score"] / 1000 for r in arm_runs]

probe = {}
for run in probe_runs:

x = [0, 1]
for shape, color, marker in [("16×64", COLORS["blue"], "o"), ("64×16", COLORS["orange"], "s")]:

Indexing that record is what the Design-Loop Card of @sec-design-loop-card exists for, and the array study is the one study in this book with enough retained evidence to fill one (@tbl-array-design-loop-card). Every entry below is transcribed from the retained package rather than composed for the table, including the fields the package left empty.

| **Card field** | **Executed systolic-array study** |
| :--- | :--- |
| **Architecture question** | Does any legal nonbaseline processing element (PE) geometry clear a 1% margin on the frozen local score against the mandatory 32 by 32 baseline, on the declared three-layer general matrix multiplication (GEMM) workload? |
| **Comparator** | The 32 by 32 baseline, rerun inside both proposal arms rather than carried across them. |
| **Permitted change** | Array rows and columns drawn from 8, 16, 32, 64, and 128, with their product not exceeding 1,024 processing elements. Dataflow, SRAM capacities, bandwidth parameters, workload, and scoring rule are frozen. |
| **Rejection checks** | The 1,024-element legality limit, the 90,000-cycle performance cutoff, and the 1% support margin, all fixed before candidate selection. |
| **Budget** | Four simulator evaluation events per proposal arm plus four shared mechanism-probe events. Twelve events were recorded and none was refused. |
| **Evidence returned** | A tie at a local score of 33,782.40 between the baseline and the 16 by 64 candidate, three lower-ranked geometries, and a transposition probe that refutes the proposed reversal. |
| **Evidence not returned** | Seed, temperature, and serving state for the model call; a repository commit binding for the runner; a validation dataset; and any independent replay. |
| **Decision status** | `awaiting_author_confirmation`. The machine-readable recommendation retains 32 by 32 for the evaluated set and closes the recorded search. |
| **Commitment authority** | Unassigned in the retained record. The technical outcome supports the recommendation above, but no human commitment is recorded. |
: **A filled card indexes what one executed study established and what it left open.** The card binds the frozen question and permitted change to the returned evidence, the missing evidence, and the approval that was never exercised. Empty fields are recorded as empty rather than omitted. {#tbl-array-design-loop-card tbl-colwidths="[24,76]"}

The last two rows distinguish the technical recommendation from approval. No person is assigned to accept the recommendation, and no acceptance is recorded. The card makes this visible without requiring a reviewer to reconstruct the chronology. Automated tooling can check and rank recommendations against technical thresholds; the person responsible for the architecture decision must still decide whether to act on them.

## Review and Decision Criteria

Evaluating an architectural candidate requires separating the proposal from its supporting rationale. A proposal may achieve high performance under specific benchmark conditions while its underlying explanation is invalid. Conversely, a flawed proposal may reflect a valid physical insight obscured by secondary tool artifacts. A proposal's pass or fail score and the validity of its physical mechanism are separate findings. A third question, how proposals would disperse across repeated sampling, the retained record cannot answer, because it holds only one model call and did not log its temperature; that measurement belongs to complete-system evaluation (@sec-evaluating-agentic-architect). What the record can test is the mechanism.

### Directional Mechanism Probe Analysis

Architectural auditing must verify whether a proposal's stated microarchitectural rationale survives empirical testing. The generative model made two claims. It predicted that a wide 16 by 64 array would outperform a tall 64 by 16 layout on the baseline workload, and it hypothesized that swapping matrix dimensions $M$ and $N$ would reverse their relative performance. The retained records uphold the first and contradict the second, and only the second was the mechanism test. In the [retained study results](https://github.com/harvard-edge/arch2/blob/f5516e52e66243c2d753191e350a5cfac56c83af/labs/examples/ai_systolic_array_study/recorded/reference/study_results.json), the original local scores of 33,782.40 versus 54,985.25 compare against transposed scores of 23,530.65 versus 25,458.11; the predicted architectural reversal does not occur. Observing a narrower performance gap under transposition fails to validate the proposed physical mechanism.

The surviving prompt copy also omits the dataflow mapping semantics necessary to interpret this hardware contrast. While retained execution logs identify SCALE-Sim 3.0.0, they omit any dependency hash or source commit tracking. The following interpretation therefore uses the $K$-height, $N$-width, and $M$-temporal mapping in the publicly tagged v3.0.0 implementation [@ScaleSimProject2025V300Source], without treating that source inspection as a replay of the retained run.

What the array comparison actually varied depends on the simulator's mapping semantics, set out in @fig-array-mapping. Weight-Stationary GEMM maps the $K$ dimension to physical array height and the $N$ dimension to array width, while matrix dimension $M$ streams temporally through the processing elements.

![**Spatial GEMM array contrasts reveal trade-offs beyond isolated aspect-ratio changes.** Based on the tagged SCALE-Sim (a cycle-level systolic array simulator) v3.0.0 implementation [@ScaleSimProject2025V300Source], Weight-Stationary GEMM maps the $K$ dimension to the physical array height and the $N$ dimension to the array width, while the $M$ dimension streams temporally through the processing elements. Because exchanging $M$ and $N$ leaves $K$ entirely unchanged, evaluating mirrored array shapes alters more than just one spatial fold count at a time.](images/fig-array-mapping){#fig-array-mapping fig-alt="A GEMM workload feeds a resident weight tile of K by N, which maps onto wide 16 by 64 and tall 64 by 16 arrays. K maps over array height and N over array width. A dashed transpose connector notes that K is unchanged, so the mirrored pair changes more than one fold count."}

The consequence for the probe is that a mirrored pair changes several tiling factors at once rather than one. Mapping a large matrix multiplication onto a fixed hardware grid requires partitioning the workload into smaller tiles. When a matrix dimension exceeds the physical array dimension, the accelerator must fold the computation, processing the data across multiple spatial passes. Consequently, altering the physical aspect ratio changes the required spatial passes across both height and width simultaneously. For the first GEMM layer, with dimensions $(M,N,K) = (128, 128, 256)$, the $16 \times 64$ array requires $\lceil 256/16 \rceil = 16$ vertical $K$-folds and $\lceil 128/64 \rceil = 2$ horizontal $N$-folds ($16 \times 2 = 32$ spatial passes).

Conversely, the $64 \times 16$ array requires $\lceil 256/64 \rceil = 4$ vertical $K$-folds and $\lceil 128/16 \rceil = 8$ horizontal $N$-folds ($4 \times 8 = 32$ spatial passes). Evaluating these multiple altered factors systematically requires mapping them across the complete workload (@tbl-systolic-folding-breakdown). Aligning diagnostic probes with simulator dataflow semantics is essential to avoid confounding hardware parameters.

| **Array Shape ($H \times W$)** | **Height Mapping ($K=256$)** | **Width Mapping ($N=128$)** | **Layer 1 Spatial Passes ($K\text{-folds} \times N\text{-folds}$)** | **Modeled DRAM Writes** | **3-Layer Total Cycles** |
| :- | :- | :- | :- | -: | -: |
| **Wide Array ($16 \times 64$)** | $\lceil 256/16 \rceil = 16\text{ vertical folds}$ | $\lceil 128/64 \rceil = 2\text{ horizontal folds}$ | $16 \times 2 = \mathbf{32\text{ passes}}$ | 409,726 | 13,917 |
| **Balanced Baseline ($32 \times 32$)** | $\lceil 256/32 \rceil = 8\text{ vertical folds}$ | $\lceil 128/32 \rceil = 4\text{ horizontal folds}$ | $8 \times 4 = \mathbf{32\text{ passes}}$ | 204,863 | 13,917 |
| **Tall Array ($64 \times 16$)** | $\lceil 256/64 \rceil = 4\text{ vertical folds}$ | $\lceil 128/16 \rceil = 8\text{ horizontal folds}$ | $4 \times 8 = \mathbf{32\text{ passes}}$ | 102,400 | 17,757 |
: **Spatial tiling and fold factor decomposition across 1,024-PE systolic array geometries.** For symmetric Layer 1 $(128, 128, 256)$, all three geometries execute exactly 32 spatial passes. Across the full 3-layer workload, the wide $16 \times 64$ geometry ties the baseline at 13,917 total cycles while SCALE-Sim reports twice as many modeled DRAM-word writes, and the tall $64 \times 16$ array needs 17,757 cycles. These totals sum the report's `Total Cycles` column, excluding its separate prefetch-inclusive column. The retained three-layer aggregates do not locate the cause of that cycle gap, which remains unresolved. {#tbl-systolic-folding-breakdown tbl-colwidths="[20,20,20,20,10,10]"}

While the model's directional prediction fails its declared test, this invalidated contrast does not establish a viable replacement mechanism. It does not prove that systolic array orientation is structurally irrelevant to overall performance. Launching a new mechanism study requires a specialized prompt with pinned mapping semantics alongside a contrast methodology that isolates and varies exactly one fold count at a time.

The retained outputs expose a separate memory question without answering it. SCALE-Sim reports 409,726 modeled DRAM-word writes for the 16 by 64 array and 204,863 for the 32 by 32 baseline, even though the two shapes tie on cycles and the frozen local score. The run set `UseRamulatorTrace = False`, so these counts describe idealized buffer traffic rather than contention-aware memory timing. Request order, tensor layout, physical address mapping, memory organization, and controller policy all remain unbound. The twofold write count therefore supports an inference that memory behavior could matter to a later decision, not a claim about bank conflicts, latency, energy, or relative physical performance.

The missing timing model matters because a row-buffer hit can proceed with a column command, whereas a row conflict requires the controller to precharge the open row, activate the requested row, and then issue the column command.[^fn-dram-timing-c08] Whether this request stream ever exercises that sequence depends on physical address mapping and controller scheduling, neither of which the retained run modeled [@KimEtAl2015Ramulator; @LuoEtAl2024Ramulator2].

### Proposed Follow-up Memory Study

**Status**: This is an author-constructed next-study contract. It is proposed, not authorized, not executed, and not part of the retained array record.

The observed tie and modeled-write difference motivate a narrower contention-aware memory study. Before dispatch, that study would freeze:

1. **Question and comparison**: Test whether the recorded write-traffic difference between the 16 by 64 candidate and 32 by 32 baseline changes a declared memory-sensitive outcome under the same workload and array configuration. The traffic difference is the observation; its cause and timing consequence remain hypotheses.
2. **Controlled memory state**: Bind request ordering, tensor layout, dataflow, physical address mapping, channel and bank organization, controller policy, timing parameters, simulator identity, and parsing rules. Neither array aspect ratio nor write count alone determines bank conflicts.
3. **Returns and stopping**: Retain commands, traces, contention and timing returns, failures, versions, costs, and a rerun of the baseline. Freeze the estimator, decision margin, budget, and stopping rule before execution.

Writing this contract does not mutate the retained study or close a design loop. Once authorized, a follow-up attempt would receive its own execution record, including any dispatch failure or tool returns. Returned evidence would then have to change the represented design state and trigger another allowed action before the operational closing test is met.

## Metric Mismatches and Proxy Discrepancies

The proposed memory study addresses what the score omitted. A second limitation concerns what the search omitted: even a more informative score would rank only the shapes actually evaluated. The fifteen legal processing-element geometries and the four-event budget for each arm reveal that coverage boundary (@tbl-array-shape-coverage). Across both arms, the runs evaluated five unique shapes (8 by 128, 16 by 64, 32 by 16, 32 by 32, and 64 by 16), leaving ten legal geometries unexecuted. Repeating candidate evaluations across proposal arms consumes simulation events without expanding architectural coverage.

| **Status** | **Exact legal shapes** | **Count** |
| - | - | -: |
| Evaluated as unique original-workload geometries | 8 by 128; 16 by 64; 32 by 16; 32 by 32; 64 by 16 | 5 |
| Not executed | 8 by 8; 8 by 16; 8 by 32; 8 by 64; 16 by 8; 16 by 16; 16 by 32; 32 by 8; 64 by 8; 128 by 8 | 10 |
: **Five evaluated geometries do not close the fifteen-shape architectural space.** While repeated arm events preserve frozen budgets, they contribute no new geometrical insights. Consequently, no retained SCALE-Sim (a cycle-level systolic array simulator) results exist for the ten remaining legal shapes. {#tbl-array-shape-coverage tbl-colwidths="[28,60,12]"}

The space is small. With fifteen legal shapes and a recorded simulator window of 19.05 seconds for twelve events, an exhaustive reference appears inexpensive, although its actual runtime remains unmeasured. It was withheld by design. The preregistration fixed a budget-matched comparison between two proposal arms, and folding a full enumeration into that record would have changed what the record tests. Without it, performance outcomes cannot be inferred for the ten unexecuted shapes, and the record cannot claim that the model tied or outperformed the complete design space; a full-space reference belongs in a separately frozen record.

Within the evaluated set, plotting cycles against modeled DRAM-word writes makes the score's omission visible (@fig-proxy-mismatch). The baseline and the wide candidate occupy the same horizontal position but different vertical positions. The tall candidate uses more cycles while reporting fewer modeled writes, exposing a trade-off that a one-number ranking cannot show.

The need to check distinct outcomes has a parallel in recovery testing. FATE and DESTINI combine failure exploration with explicit checks for outcomes such as availability and data loss [@GunawiEtAl2011FATEDestini]. The analogous caution here is that a favorable scalar score leaves unscored properties unresolved.

::: {.callout-law title="The Whac-a-Mole Regression Effect"}
**The Caution:** Optimizing a single scalar metric can hide trade-offs in quantities the score omits. Those quantities need their own checks; improvement in one metric does not establish their acceptability or imply that they must regress.

**The Hardware Trap:** Reading a tied score as interchangeable behavior hides the write-count difference. That omission becomes consequential if a later decision depends on the memory system, even though this run does not determine the physical consequence.

**The Architectural Antidote:** Freeze every decision quantity that the scoped claim needs before execution, and keep modeled returns distinct from physical measurements. A future memory study must test contention, timing, and energy under its own bound configuration rather than reading those consequences out of the retained SCALE-Sim write counts (@sec-law-whac-a-mole in @sec-appendix-b-laws-paradoxes).
:::


```{python}
#| label: fig-proxy-mismatch
#| fig-cap: |
#|   **Modeled traffic exposes model-local dominance masked by the scalar score.** Across retained SCALE-Sim (a cycle-level systolic array simulator) total cycles (horizontal axis, lower is better) and modeled DRAM-word writes (vertical axis, lower is better), the 32 by 32 baseline and shared 16 by 64 candidate tie at 13,917 cycles while reporting 204,863 and 409,726 modeled writes, respectively. The baseline therefore dominates the candidate only across these two retained SCALE-Sim (a cycle-level systolic array simulator) quantities. This post-run observation does not alter the frozen study outcome or establish physical traffic, contention, timing, or energy [@RajEtAl2025ScaleSimV3].
#| out-width: "100%"
#| fig-alt: "Scatter plot of evaluated systolic array shapes across retained SCALE-Sim (a cycle-level systolic array simulator) total cycles and modeled DRAM-word writes, showing the 32 by 32 baseline and 16 by 64 candidate tied at 13,917 cycles while reporting 204,863 and 409,726 modeled writes, respectively."

import json
from pathlib import Path
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
import _python.plots as _ap
from _python.plots import COLORS, apply_style

apply_style()

_root = Path(_ap.__file__).resolve().parents[2]
result_path = _root / "labs/examples/ai_systolic_array_study/recorded/reference/study_results.json"
result = json.loads(result_path.read_text(encoding="utf-8"))
arm_runs = [r for r in result["evaluations"] if r["arm"] in {"model", "conventional"}]

fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(5.6, 3.5))
fig.subplots_adjust(left=0.18, right=0.95, top=0.95, bottom=0.15)

ax.set_xlabel("SCALE-Sim (a cycle-level systolic array simulator) total cycles (lower is better)", fontsize=6.5)
ax.set_ylabel("Modeled DRAM-word writes (lower is better)", fontsize=6.5)

seen = set()
for r in arm_runs:
    key = (r["workload_id"], r["array_rows"], r["array_cols"])
    if key in seen:
        continue
    seen.add(key)

    cid = r["candidate_id"]
    cycles = r["metrics"]["total_cycles"]
    dram_writes = r["metrics"]["dram_writes"]
    label = cid.replace("model_baseline_", "").replace("ai_wide_", "").replace("ai_extreme_", "").replace("ai_compact_", "").replace("conventional_baseline_", "").replace("heuristic_", "")

    if "32x32" in label:
        ax.plot(cycles, dram_writes, marker="o", markersize=5, color=COLORS["blue"])
        ax.text(cycles + 300, dram_writes - 12000, f"Baseline {label}", color=COLORS["ink"], fontsize=5.5, ha="left", va="top")
    elif "16x64" in label:
        ax.plot(cycles, dram_writes, marker="X", markersize=5, color=COLORS["red"])
        ax.text(cycles + 300, dram_writes + 15000, f"Shared candidate\n{label}", color=COLORS["ink"], fontsize=5.5, ha="left", va="bottom")
    else:
        ax.plot(cycles, dram_writes, marker="s", markersize=4, color=COLORS["orange"], alpha=0.6)
        ax.text(cycles + 300, dram_writes, label, color=COLORS["ink"], fontsize=5, ha="left", va="center", alpha=0.7)

baseline_cycles = next(
    r["metrics"]["total_cycles"]
    for r in arm_runs
    if r["workload_id"] == "original"
    and r["array_rows"] == 32
    and r["array_cols"] == 32
)
ax.axvline(x=baseline_cycles, color=COLORS["grid"], linestyle="--", linewidth=0.8, zorder=0)
ax.set_xlim(12800, 27800)

ax.tick_params(axis="both", labelsize=5.9, length=2.5, width=0.6, pad=2)
ax.grid(True, color=COLORS["grid"], linewidth=0.55, zorder=0)
for spine in ["top", "right"]:
    ax.spines[spine].set_visible(False)
ax.spines["left"].set_color(COLORS["ink"])
ax.spines["bottom"].set_color(COLORS["ink"])

plt.show()
```

The baseline dominates the wide candidate across these two plotted quantities: equal cycles and fewer modeled writes. The tall candidate instead trades more cycles for fewer writes. Neither observation changes the original score-based tie, because the study never declared a rule for choosing across these axes. A follow-up could retain the original score for comparability, add a justified traffic objective, or adopt a different scoring rule. Freezing that choice before execution would let the next record answer its own question without rewriting this one's result.

## Technical Boundaries of Architectural Loop Execution

Comparing the unexecuted Level-2 cache plan with the executed systolic-array experiment shows why different stops support different conclusions. The cache study lacks an executable path; the array study has returned measurements whose coverage, score, and provenance limit the recommendation. Comparing them exposes those limits without resolving either study's missing work.

The array record stops at five boundaries, and each names a next step rather than a result:

- **Tie**: Returned scores demonstrate no advantage for model-guided proposals over the fixed heuristic under equal simulator-event budgets, retaining 32 by 32 for the evaluated set. Broader selection claims require a separately frozen full-space reference.
- **Failed mechanism**: Transposition results reject the predicted performance reversal without offering a replacement mechanism; isolating the true hardware behavior requires a newly frozen study with pinned mapping semantics.
- **Omitted metric**: Modeled DRAM-word counts expose a returned quantity absent from the frozen score. This post-run observation cannot alter the frozen outcome; it can only motivate a separately justified modeled-traffic axis or a future contention-aware study.
- **Provenance gap**: Missing exact prompt and simulator identities prevent establishing an exact historical replay and limit causal attribution. A separately documented rerun could test the available package under newly recorded conditions.
- **Pending decision**: The machine-readable technical recommendation retains 32 by 32 for the evaluated set, concluding technical search while leaving the architecture decision to an as-yet unassigned person.

Read under the same four judgments applied to the cache record (@tbl-cache-judgments), the two records diverge in every column (@tbl-lighthouse-return).

| **Record** | **Architecture outcome** | **AI contribution** | **Mechanism** | **Stopping and action** |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| mobile XR cache path | Unresolved. | Not tested. | Untested. | Stop before execution. |
| Separate executed array study | No nonbaseline design clears local margin. | No advantage under equal event budgets. | Reversal prediction fails; no replacement. | Retains 32 by 32 for evaluated set. |
: **The two records stop at different technical boundaries.** The mobile XR cache path never reaches execution, while the separate retained array study executes only a narrow simulator comparison with no recorded authorization for acceptance or rejection. Because these are not cohesive stages of a single end-to-end Lighthouse run, neither result can finalize the other. {#tbl-lighthouse-return tbl-colwidths="[18,21,20,21,20]"}

These unresolved boundaries (ranking ties, refuted physical mechanisms, omitted memory metrics, and provenance gaps) define the exact scope for follow-up investigations rather than dead ends. However, none of these follow-ups ran in the original iteration, and each demands its own separately frozen experimental protocol before execution. A new study cannot append steps to an existing record without declaring a fresh baseline, frozen budgets, and explicit decision criteria.

Both records leave the system-level questions open. The retained SCALE-Sim configuration evaluates isolated array geometries. Synthetic GEMM matrices bypass compiler lowering to vector pipelines, contention-aware shared DRAM simulation, power-domain isolation, formal property verification, and chiplet interconnects. Although the broader SCALE-Sim v3 framework supports memory and energy integration [@RajEtAl2025ScaleSimV3], the retained run restricted execution to standalone PE array traffic. Neither record executes an identified XR workload, validates tail deadlines under deployed conditions, or exercises the runtime, host vector cores, shared memory path, sensors, or display engine. The array result therefore cannot resolve the cache sizing decision for XRBench [@KwonEtAl2023XRBench], SPEC CPU [@SPEC2017CPU], or MLPerf [@ReddiEtAl2020MLPerfInference], satisfy the 3\ W envelope, or close the Lighthouse design loop. Physical design checks across timing closure, design rule checking (DRC), power delivery network integrity,[^fn-pdn-integrity-c08] and thermal signoff remain unexecuted. Naming a check in an architectural plan is never a substitute for running it.

::: {.callout-design-principle title="Claim Only What Checked Records Support"}
**The principle:** An architecture evaluation loop must bound its claims strictly to what its executed, checked tool records demonstrate.

**The application:** Unexecuted plans do not provide measured results. Partial simulation logs and budget-limited ties can support only the local claims their retained checks establish; they do not substitute for physical or silicon evidence.
:::

## A Hypothetical Feedback Iteration

The two records stop before returned evidence drives another design action. To see the missing step, consider an author-constructed example of an instruction-design loop for a ChaCha20 cryptographic kernel on a VexRiscv microcontroller. This example has no retained execution behind it. Suppose an architect authorizes exploration across the software/hardware instruction interface to reduce kernel cycles under an illustrative 15,000 gate-equivalent area limit, with fixed functional and timing checks and a bounded retry budget. Generating and evaluating alternatives across that interface places the proposed work within AI-native scope. The architect still decides whether the resulting evidence justifies adopting a candidate.

A generative component might propose a custom `ROTL` (rotate left) instruction, modify the SpinalHDL implementation, and adapt the software to use it. The environment would synthesize the design with Yosys and analyze the resulting timing with OpenSTA. Suppose the first return reports an illustrative -300\ ps of slack[^fn-negative-slack-c08] along the new rotation path. The environment would retain the full report and expose the failing path and timing constraint in a structured return. The represented design state would then contain a specific failed check, giving the next proposal a concrete constraint to address.

Within the authorized budget, the component could respond by inserting a pipeline register and requesting re-evaluation. That evidence-driven revision and subsequent tool action would close the feedback loop. It would not yet establish an improved architecture. The register could shorten a combinational path while adding instruction latency, area, or pipeline hazards, so the next iteration would need functional checks, a matched Verilator cycle comparison, area accounting, and timing analysis under the declared constraints. A passing set of returns could support a scoped recommendation; a failure could motivate another permitted revision or a technical stop. Routed feasibility would still require the relevant physical-design checks, and commitment would remain with the named human authority.

The distinction matters for reading the preceding records. Loop closure describes how evidence changes subsequent work. Success describes whether that work meets the declared architecture criteria. A loop can close and still reject its candidate, just as a fixed sweep can yield a useful technical result without closing an adaptive loop.

## Open Questions

The two records leave unresolved how to constrain exploration physically, allocate diagnostic work, combine subsystem evidence, and decide whether a tie warrants further study.

- **How can early physical constraints guide exploration without excluding viable designs?** Deriving legal banks and array geometries makes a candidate concrete enough to evaluate, but does not establish that it can be routed. Multiplexing delays and routing congestion[^fn-routing-congestion-c08] may emerge only when surrounding blocks and wires are included. The unresolved question is how to combine constructive derivation rules with selective physical-design feedback, measuring both the cost of advancing infeasible candidates and the risk of discarding feasible ones before simulation.

- **How should a design system divide its compute between finding better candidates and testing their explanations?** A fixed simulation budget forces a trade-off between evaluating more configurations and running diagnostic hypothesis tests. A favorable score can coexist with a failed explanation, leaving the system uncertain whether to search nearby designs or investigate an artifact of the simulator or compiler. Research must determine when evidence gathered during search justifies shifting effort toward diagnosis, and how that adaptation can preserve an interpretable comparison with a conventional search under the same total budget.

- **When can separately evaluated subsystems support a system-level conclusion?** Separate compute-array, memory-hierarchy, and interconnect studies make exploration tractable, but local results can omit interactions through shared resources. Network-on-chip contention, bank conflicts, and memory-latency tails can change which subsystem design is preferable after integration. The open issue is which interface assumptions and composition bounds can limit that uncertainty well enough for a stated system decision, and which interactions require full-system co-simulation before a local recommendation can advance.

- **When does stopping a tied study produce more insight than breaking the tie?** A tie under a frozen score leaves open whether the designs are equivalent for the intended decision or differ in quantities the score omitted. Repeating a deterministic comparison need not reveal that difference, while changing the workload, metric, or model asks a new question. The unresolved issue is how to estimate the decision value of that additional evidence: when is accepting a scoped tie justified, and when is a higher-fidelity study worth its cost?

## Summary

An architectural claim can reach only as far as its retained evidence and qualified checks. This chapter put that rule to work on two records that deliberately do not compose. The cache record is a specification with a dispatch condition and no execution behind it, so it supports a question, a comparator, and a stopping category, and nothing about how any capacity behaves. The array record ran its preregistered budget to completion and returned a tie against a modest fixed heuristic, a refuted directional explanation, and a technical stop that retains the 32 by 32 baseline for the five shapes it evaluated. Read under the four judgments of @tbl-cache-judgments, the two records answer differently, and neither answer can be borrowed to fill the other.

Each diagnostic return names a possible next study rather than an executed next action. A tie under matched budgets may justify a separately frozen full-space reference, which appears inexpensive here given the short recorded simulator window. A refuted explanation motivates an isolating probe with pinned dataflow mapping. A provenance gap calls for re-execution with the prompt, container hash, and toolchain lock recorded. None of those follow-ups ran, and rescoring the retained study cannot substitute for them. The hypothetical instruction-design example makes the missing transition concrete: a failed timing check changes the candidate and triggers a new evaluation, closing a loop without guaranteeing that the revised candidate will pass.

::: {.callout-takeaways}
- **Claims bounded by evidence class.** Prospective specifications, executed simulator records, physical-design results, and silicon measurements support different claims, and the two records here never cross that line.
- **Prospective parameter binding.** The array record froze its workload, legal shapes, score, margin, and budgets before the first simulator event, which is what lets its tie be read as a result rather than a tuning artifact.
- **Four separate judgments.** Architecture outcome, study-local AI contribution, mechanism status, and the action the record permits are separate judgments, and an aggregate score cannot carry them.
- **Modeled traffic as a next-study signal.** The twofold write-count difference exposes a quantity the frozen score omitted; it establishes nothing about contention, timing, energy, or physical ranking until a separately frozen memory study tests it.
- **Feedback must change subsequent work.** A proposed follow-up is still a plan. In the hypothetical instruction example, a returned timing failure prompts a generated hardware revision and another evaluation; that closes the loop while leaving the revised candidate's success unresolved.
:::

The cache plan, the executed array sweep, and the hypothetical feedback sequence have different evidence states. What they share is a bounded question whose assumptions determine what can travel to another study. The next chapter (@sec-loop-patterns-across-stack) asks which parts of a plan or retained result remain usable when the workload, tools, or decision changes.



[^fn-xr-workload-c08]: **Prospective XR Workload Requirement**: The 120\ Hz sensor rate and strict 8.33\ ms frame deadline are chosen requirements for this unexecuted study. They are not measurements or requirements established here from an XRBench trace; a workload snapshot with the specified frame boundaries still needs to be bound before dispatch.

[^fn-pvt-corners-c08]: **Process, voltage, and temperature (PVT) corners**: In physical chip design, PVT corners specify combinations of manufacturing-process variation, supply voltage, and operating temperature (e.g., slow process, low voltage, high temperature). A result supports claims only about the properties analyzed under the selected corners and modeling assumptions.

[^fn-dram-timing-c08]: **DRAM Timing and Row Conflicts**: Modern DRAM is organized into 2D arrays. Accessing data requires activating an entire row and loading it into a fast "row buffer." If a subsequent memory request targets a different row in the same bank, the controller must first "precharge" (close) the active row before activating the new one. This sequence incurs a significant latency penalty known as a row conflict.

[^fn-weight-stationary-c08]: **Weight-Stationary Dataflow**: An accelerator design pattern where neural network weights are pinned to local registers within a systolic array, while activations stream across them, minimizing expensive memory reads.

[^fn-timing-closure-c08]: **Timing Closure**: The process of modifying a physical chip design until all electrical signals arrive at their destinations within the exact time windows required by the clock frequency, preventing data corruption from setup or hold time violations.

[^fn-routing-congestion-c08]: **Routing Congestion**: A physical layout condition where too many metal interconnect wires must traverse a restricted die area. Congestion can force design software to take long, circuitous paths that ruin performance, or fail to wire the chip entirely.

[^fn-pdn-integrity-c08]: **power delivery network (PDN) integrity**: Ensuring the on-chip mesh of power wires can reliably supply the required voltage to all billions of transistors simultaneously without dangerous voltage drops (IR drop) or long-term metal degradation (electromigration).

[^fn-negative-slack-c08]: **Negative Slack**: In timing analysis, "slack" is the time difference between when a signal actually arrives and when it is required to arrive. Negative slack indicates a timing violation where the signal is too slow for the target clock speed, causing computation errors.
